description: Training Data Poisoning Attack Attackers could exploit weak access controls or missing validation on the S3 input bucket to upload malicious training data or modify existing data. This could lead to the training process producing models with intentionally compromised behavior. An attacker gains write access to the input data bucket through misconfigured IAM permissions or compromised credentials, then uploads carefully crafted malicious training samples that cause the model to learn unwanted behaviors or backdoors.
references: owaspTop10: A08:2021-Software and Data Integrity Failures
recommendation: Implement strict access controls and validation for training data
recommendation: Implement data integrity verification system

description: Side-Channel Attack on Inferentia Instances Side-channel attacks exploit shared hardware resources to leak information about model parameters or execution patterns. This could allow extraction of sensitive model information or training data. An attacker deploys a malicious workload on the same physical infrastructure as the Inferentia instance, then uses timing or power analysis to extract information about the model during inference.

Unauthorized Model Repository Access Insufficient access controls or overly permissive IAM roles could allow unauthorized access to the model repository, leading to intellectual property theft or model tampering. An attacker exploits overly permissive IAM roles or misconfigured bucket policies to download proprietary models or replace legitimate models with malicious versions.

description: Insecure Instance Configuration Misconfigured EC2 instances, particularly those with public SSH access or outdated software, could be compromised and used as entry points into the platform. An attacker exploits the permissive SSH access (0.0.0.0/0) configured in the development environment to gain unauthorized access to training instances.
